ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Talk It Out, Help Is Here

fullPassage:
Talk It Out, Help Is Here

Host: On today's show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe called Friendship Benches. We have two special guests. First, please welcome the founder of the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon Chibanda. Can you tell us what inspired you to come up with the program?

Dr. Chibanda: Sure. The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I had never considered such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and receive medical treatment. Furthermore, there has been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years. When the Friendship Bench program started in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists serving Zimbabwe's population of over twelve million people. I needed to find a way to bring psychiatry into the community.

Host: Oh, so that was the beginning of it. Could you explain to us how the Friendship Bench program works?

Dr. Chibanda: Certainly. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are free and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with emotional support.

Host: What a wonderful idea! How did these amazing grandmothers become a part of your program?

Dr. Chibanda: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions. They are also very reliable, which is important for our efforts to support mental health. At the beginning, we started with only fourteen volunteer grandmothers. But today, there are thousands of grandmothers who have been trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in Zimbabwe.

Host: That's interesting! What happens after patients complete their sessions with the grandmothers?

Dr. Chibanda: When the sessions with the grandmothers are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group made up of former patients of the program. The members of these groups can easily relate to and support one another. This is because most of them come from the same community and have experienced similar struggles.

Host: That sounds like a great way to continue the support and build a sense of community. And the program has been incredibly successful, right?

Dr. Chibanda: That's correct. In 2022, we provided face-to-face counseling to about 90,000 patients in Zimbabwe. Now, Friendship Benches are available in more than twenty different regions around the country. Our vision is for everyone to have a Friendship Bench within walking distance, and we are working hard to make it happen. We've also started expanding the program, and we now offer online counseling through an app. This has helped us reach even more people.

Host: That's really amazing! Thank you for your time, Dr. Chibanda. Now let's hear from one of the grandmothers who volunteer for the program. Can you introduce yourself and tell us how you got involved with the Friendship Bench program?

Grandma Moyo: Hello, my name is Judith Moyo, but people call me Grandma Moyo. I'm 76 years old, and I have been volunteering for the Friendship Bench program for about eight years. I joined the program because many people in my community struggle with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it. I knew that I could help heal their wounded hearts by supporting them.

Host: That's very kind of you. Can you tell us about your experience as a grandmother for the Friendship Bench program?

Grandma Moyo: It's been wonderful. Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of. I've seen how it can make a difference in people's lives. One patient of mine, a nineteen-year-old girl, was going through a difficult time after her mom passed away. I counseled her and helped her begin her recovery journey. Now her life is back on track, and she has even started her own business! Cases like this make me so proud to be part of the program. It is such a rewarding experience to help people make positive changes in their lives.

Host: Thanks for sharing your experiences with us today, Grandma Moyo. It's truly inspiring to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had. And it's all thanks to the hard work of people like you and Dr. Chibanda.

questions.passage: The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely (A)[depressed / impressed]. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to (B)[afford / avoid] the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I had never (C)[considered / committed] such a problem before.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 제 환자 중 한 명이 심하게 우울해졌습니다. 버스비를 감당할 수 없어 도움을 받지 못했습니다. 이런 문제를 생각해 본 적이 없어 충격을 받았습니다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) depressed: 환자가 심하게 '우울'해진 것. impressed(감명받은)는 문맥과 맞지 않음. ✅ (B) afford: 'afford the bus ride'(버스비를 감당하다). avoid(피하다)는 문맥 불일치. ✅ (C) considered: 'had never considered'(생각해 본 적 없다). committed(저지르다)는 problem과 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: afford: ~할 여유가 되다. can't afford + 명사/to-V 형태로 자주 출제.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide (A)[accessible / excessive] mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or (B)[anxiety / curiosity]. The sessions are free and are provided by (C)[respected / restricted] elderly women from the community.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 접근하기 쉬운 정신 건강 서비스를 제공하기 위해 만들어졌다. 우울증이나 불안과 같은 문제를 겪는 사람들에게 대화 치료를 제공한다. 존경받는 노인 여성들이 세션을 진행한다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) accessible: '접근 가능한' 정신 건강 서비스. excessive(과도한)는 문맥과 반대. ✅ (B) anxiety: depression과 나란히 쓰이는 정신 건강 용어. curiosity(호기심)는 질병이 아님. ✅ (C) respected: '존경받는' 노인 여성. restricted(제한된)는 사람을 수식하기 부적절.
det.tip: accessible(접근 가능한) vs excessive(과도한): 접두사가 비슷하지만 의미가 전혀 다르다.

questions.passage: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, (A)[empathy / apathy], and the ability to (B)[engage / escape] in meaningful discussions. They are also very (C)[reliable / relative], which is important for our efforts to support mental health.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 뛰어난 경청 기술, 공감, 그리고 의미 있는 토론에 참여할 수 있는 능력을 갖추고 있다. 매우 믿을 수 있는 분들이다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) empathy: 상담가의 자질로 '공감'. apathy(무관심)는 정반대. ✅ (B) engage: 'engage in discussions'(토론에 참여하다). escape(탈출하다)는 문맥 불일치. ✅ (C) reliable: '믿을 수 있는'. relative(상대적인/친척)는 형용사로 쓰일 때 '상대적인'이라 문맥과 안 맞음.
det.tip: empathy(공감) vs apathy(무관심): -pathy는 '감정'을 뜻하는 어근. em-(안으로) vs a-(없음).

questions.passage: One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to ①<u>afford</u> the bus ride to the hospital. This ②<u>shocked</u> me, as I had never considered such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and receive medical ③<u>entertainment</u>. Furthermore, there has been a ④<u>lack</u> of psychiatrists in the country for many years.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 교통비를 내고 의학적 치료를 받는 것이 어렵다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①afford: '감당하다' → 문맥 적절. ✅ ②shocked: 충격을 주었다 → 문맥 적절. ❌ ③entertainment: '오락'이 아니라 원문은 treatment(치료). 의학적 치료를 받는 맥락에서 entertainment는 부적절. ✅ ④lack: '부족' → 문맥 적절.
det.tip: treatment(치료) vs entertainment(오락): -ment 접미사를 공유하지만 의미가 전혀 다르다. treat(치료하다) + -ment, entertain(즐겁게 하다) + -ment.

questions.passage: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply ①<u>connected</u> to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in ②<u>meaningful</u> discussions. At the beginning, we started with only fourteen ③<u>volunteer</u> grandmothers. They are also very ④<u>unreliable</u>, which is important for our efforts to support mental health.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 매우 믿음직한(reliable) 분들인데, 이것이 정신 건강 지원 노력에 중요하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①connected: 지역 사회에 깊이 '연결된' → 적절. ✅ ②meaningful: '의미 있는' 토론 → 적절. ✅ ③volunteer: '자원봉사자' 할머니 → 적절. ❌ ④unreliable: 원문은 reliable(믿을 수 있는). 정신 건강 지원에 중요하려면 '믿을 수 있어야' 하므로 unreliable(믿을 수 없는)은 반대 의미.
det.tip: reliable(믿을 수 있는) ↔ unreliable(믿을 수 없는): 접두사 un-이 반의어를 만든다.

questions.passage: I joined the program because many people in my community ①<u>struggle</u> with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it. Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ②<u>proud</u> of. I knew that I could help heal their ③<u>wounded</u> hearts by supporting them. I've seen how it can make a ④<u>difference</u> in people's lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정신 건강 문제에 대한 도움을 구하는 것은 부끄러워할(ashamed) 일이 아닙니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①struggle: 정신 건강 문제로 '고심하다' → 적절. ❌ ②proud: 원문은 ashamed(부끄러운). 'nothing to be ashamed of(부끄러워할 일이 아닌)'인데, proud(자랑스러운)로 바꾸면 '자랑스러워할 일이 아닌'이 되어 문맥이 반대. ✅ ③wounded: '상처받은' 마음 → 적절. ✅ ④difference: 'make a difference(변화를 만들다)' → 적절.
det.tip: nothing to be ashamed of: ~에 대해 부끄러워할 것이 없다. be ashamed of(~를 부끄러워하다)를 부정한 표현.

questions.passage: In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and receive medical treatment. Furthermore, there has been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years. When the Friendship Bench program started in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists serving Zimbabwe's population of over twelve million people. I needed to find a way to bring __________ into the community. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정신의학을 지역 사회에 도입할 방법을 찾아야 했다.
det.analysis: 정신과 의사가 부족한 상황에서 '정신의학(psychiatry)'을 지역 사회에 도입하는 것이 논리적. ① entertainment(오락), ② transportation(교통), ③ agriculture(농업)는 모두 문맥과 무관.
det.tip: psychiatry(정신의학) — psychiatrist(정신과 의사)의 학문명. psych-(마음) + -iatry(치료).

questions.passage: The program has been incredibly successful. When the sessions with the grandmothers are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group made up of __________ patients of the program. The members of these groups can easily relate to and support one another. This is because most of them come from the same community and have experienced similar struggles.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 프로그램의 이전 환자들로 구성된 커뮤니티 지원 그룹에 참여하도록 권장된다.
det.analysis: 세션을 마친 후 참여하는 그룹이므로 이미 치료를 받은 '이전(former)' 환자로 구성. ① current(현재의)는 아직 치료 중인 환자. ③ foreign(외국의), ④ potential(잠재적인)은 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: former(이전의) ↔ current(현재의). former patients = 이전 환자, 과거에 치료를 받았던 사람들.

questions.passage: I counseled her and helped her begin her recovery journey. Now her life is back on track, and she has even started her own business! Cases like this make me so proud to be part of the program. It is such a __________ experience to help people make positive changes in their lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람들이 삶에서 긍정적인 변화를 만들도록 돕는 것은 정말 보람된 경험이다.
det.analysis: 자랑스럽게 여기며 긍정적 변화를 언급하는 맥락에서 '보람된(rewarding)'이 적절. ② demanding(힘든), ③ overwhelming(압도적인), ④ disappointing(실망스러운)은 긍정적 맥락과 불일치.
det.tip: rewarding(보람 있는): reward(보상) + -ing. 노력의 결과가 만족스러울 때 사용.

questions.passage: One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to <u>afford</u> the bus ride to the hospital.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 afford와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 버스비를 감당하다.
det.analysis: afford = '~할 여유가 되다, ~을 감당하다'. 여기서는 버스비를 '지불할 여유가 없다'는 의미이므로 pay for(지불하다)가 가장 가까움. ① avoid(피하다), ② allow(허락하다), ④ depend on(의존하다)은 의미 불일치.
det.tip: afford: (비용을) 감당하다. can't afford = ~할 여유가 없다.

questions.passage: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the <u>qualities</u> of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 qualities와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 상담가로서의 모든 자질을 갖추고 있다.
det.analysis: qualities = '자질, 특성'. 경청 기술, 공감 등 상담가로서의 특성을 나열하므로 traits(특성)가 가장 가까움. ① quantities(양), ② qualifications(자격), ③ standards(기준)는 의미 불일치.
det.tip: quality의 두 가지 의미: ① 품질(셀 수 없음) ② 자질/특성(셀 수 있음, 복수형 qualities).

questions.passage: We've also started expanding the program, and we now offer online counseling through an app. This has helped us <u>reach</u> even more people.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 reach와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 훨씬 더 많은 사람들에게 다가가다.
det.analysis: reach = '~에게 다가가다, 접근하다'. 온라인 상담으로 더 많은 사람에게 '접근'하는 맥락에서 connect with(~와 연결되다)가 가장 가까움. ① touch(만지다), ③ arrive at(도착하다), ④ extend(확장하다)는 사람에 대한 접근 의미가 약함.
det.tip: reach + 사람: ~에게 다가가다/연락하다. reach + 장소: ~에 도착하다. 문맥에 따라 의미가 달라짐.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide <u>accessible</u> mental health services.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 accessible과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 접근 가능한 정신 건강 서비스.
det.analysis: accessible = '접근 가능한'. 반의어는 unavailable(이용 불가능한). ② affordable(감당 가능한)는 비용 관련. ③ visible(보이는), ④ acceptable(수용 가능한)은 반의어가 아님.
det.tip: accessible(접근 가능한) ↔ inaccessible/unavailable. access(접근) + -ible(~할 수 있는).

questions.passage: I counseled her and helped her begin her <u>recovery</u> journey. Now her life is back on track.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 recovery와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 회복의 여정을 시작했다.
det.analysis: recovery = '회복'. 반의어는 decline(쇠퇴, 악화). ① discovery(발견)는 recover와 어원이 다름. ② improvement(개선)은 유의어에 가까움. ③ progress(진전)도 긍정적 의미.
det.tip: recovery(회복) ↔ decline(쇠퇴). recover = re-(다시) + cover(덮다) → 원래 상태로 돌아가다.

questions.passage: I've seen how it can make a <u>difference</u> in people's lives. One patient of mine, a nineteen-year-old girl, was going through a difficult time after her mom passed away.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 difference가 다음 중 어떤 의미로 쓰였는지 고르시오.

det.korean: 그것이 사람들의 삶에 어떻게 변화를 가져올 수 있는지 보았다.
det.analysis: 'make a difference'는 '변화를 만들다, 차이를 가져오다'라는 관용 표현. 여기서 difference는 단순한 '차이'가 아니라 '긍정적 변화/영향'을 뜻함. ① 차이점(일반적 의미), ③ 의견 불일치, ④ 수량 차이는 모두 이 문맥과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: make a difference: 변화를 만들다, 중요한 영향을 미치다. It makes no difference: 상관없다.

questions.passage: Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of.
questions.stem: 다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어를 고르시오: "feeling embarrassed or guilty about something"

det.korean: 무언가에 대해 당혹스러워하거나 죄책감을 느끼는 → ashamed(부끄러운).
det.analysis: 영영풀이 'feeling embarrassed or guilty about something'은 ashamed(부끄러운)의 정의. ① inspired(영감을 받은), ② depressed(우울한), ④ wounded(상처입은)는 의미 불일치.
det.tip: ashamed: be ashamed of ~(~을 부끄러워하다). shame(수치) → ashamed(수치스러운).

questions.passage: It is such a rewarding experience to help people make positive changes in their lives. It's truly inspiring to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had.
questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 올바른 형태를 쓰시오.

The Friendship Bench program provides __________ support to patients. [emotion]

det.korean: 우정 벤치 프로그램은 환자들에게 정서적 지원을 제공한다.
det.analysis: 명사 support를 수식하려면 형용사 형태가 필요. emotion(감정, 명사) → emotional(감정적인, 형용사). '-al' 접미사가 명사를 형용사로 바꿈.
det.tip: emotion(명사: 감정) → emotional(형용사: 감정적인) → emotionally(부사: 감정적으로). 명사 앞에는 형용사가 온다.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. Grandmothers have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills and empathy.
questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 올바른 형태를 쓰시오.

The grandmothers are __________ connected to the community. [deep]

det.korean: 할머니들은 지역 사회와 깊이 연결되어 있다.
det.analysis: 동사 connected를 수식하려면 부사 형태가 필요. deep(깊은, 형용사) → deeply(깊이, 부사). '-ly' 접미사가 형용사를 부사로 바꿈.
det.tip: deep(형용사/부사) vs deeply(부사): deep은 물리적 깊이, deeply는 추상적·감정적 깊이에 주로 사용. deeply connected = 깊이 연결된.

questions.passage: On today's show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe called __________. We have two special guests. First, please welcome the founder of the program, Dr. Dixon Chibanda. Can you tell us what inspired you to come up with the program? The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 짐바브웨의 특별한 공원 벤치인 우정 벤치에 대해 알아보겠습니다.
det.analysis: 원문에서 프로그램 이름이 'Friendship Benches'로 명시되어 있음. 나머지는 원문에 없는 이름.
det.tip: Friendship Bench: 짐바브웨의 실제 정신 건강 프로그램. 공원 벤치에서 대화 치료를 제공하는 것이 핵심.

questions.passage: The program has been incredibly successful. In 2022, we provided face-to-face counseling to about 90,000 patients in Zimbabwe. Now, Friendship Benches are available in more than twenty different regions around the country. Our __________ is for everyone to have a Friendship Bench within walking distance, and we are working hard to make it happen. We've also started expanding the program.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 저희의 비전은 모두가 걸어서 갈 수 있는 거리에 우정 벤치를 갖는 것이다.
det.analysis: 원문 'Our vision is for everyone to have ~'에서 vision(비전)이 사용됨. ① concern(걱정), ③ solution(해결책), ④ complaint(불만)는 모두 문맥과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: vision: 미래에 대한 구상이나 목표. 'Our vision is ~'는 조직의 목표를 밝히는 표현.
